The wordmark

There is no drawn logotype. The wordmark is the typeface.

Afterglow

Instrument Serif 400, tracking 0. Clear space is the cap height of the A on every side. Minimum 96 px on screen, 24 mm in print.

Six ways to break it

Do not recolour

Outside the four stages and the two text neutrals.

Do not stretch

No horizontal or vertical scaling, ever.

Do not outline

No stroke, no shadow, no glow. Shadow is not in the system.

Do not stack

One line. The word does not break.

Do not set small on the fall

Below 24 px it fails its floor somewhere on the ramp.

Do not substitute

If the face is unavailable the wordmark is set as an image, not in a fallback.

The fall

The gradient is an asset with a specification, not an effect applied by eye.

Gold to violet. Never reversed.

#D8B2600%#BC6F4C30%#893A5060%#341D5E84%#08080895%#BF15B7100%

Border is rgba(192,192,192,0.22), a hairline. No neutral is a stage and no stage is a neutral.

  • Gold to violet, top to bottom or left to right. Never reversed, because the one thing the ramp says is that the light deepens.
  • Interpolated in sRGB. Specifying it in another space changes every intermediate value and the measured ratios stop holding.
  • Four stages fall to the void and end on a sliver of #BF15B7. No stage may be added, moved or removed.
  • Nothing smaller than 24 px of type sits directly on it. Type on the fall uses the floor for the darkest value it crosses.
  • In print it is a four-colour build or a gradient mesh; it is not two spot inks, which cannot hold the middle.

Grid and the one rule

Twelve columns in both media, one spacing base that divides the type base.

The one rule

No state change brightens.

Hover, focus and active deepen or shift hue and never lighten. In print and film a later panel is never lighter than the one before it. The one rule here that can be checked in a diff.

Radius

0

Square. Restraint and a dark ground point there.

none

450 ms

cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.2, 1). Ends at its destination, never passes it.

Art direction

One light source, and it is falling.

The palette is a description of light at a particular hour. Images are made to match it rather than graded toward it afterwards.

  1. One light source, and it is falling.

    Images are made at the end of the day or lit to look as though they were.

  2. The upper quartile of an image's lightness sits at or below the gold of last light, L 0.781.

    Up to a quarter of the frame may pass it; the rest may not.

  3. Warm to cool across a set, never back.

    A sequence follows the ramp in the same direction the ramp runs.

  4. Grade toward the stages rather than to neutral.

    The palette is where the shadows and the highlights land.

  5. Nothing is brightened in post.

    Exposure is lifted at capture or the frame is not used.

Misuse

Six ways to break the five rules, beside a frame cut from the brand. Each tile is built from tokens; the photograph is the real thing.

Two light sources

Breaks one light source, and it is falling.

Flat light

Breaks one light source, and it is falling: nothing falls.

Over-lit frame

Breaks the upper quartile at or below gold: over a quarter of it passes.

Reversed set

Breaks warm to cool, never back.

Graded to neutral

Breaks grade toward the stages rather than to neutral.

Lifted in post

Breaks nothing is brightened in post: the shadows are raised.

Production

  • The fall prints as a four-colour build or a gradient mesh. Two spot inks cannot hold the middle of the ramp.
  • Uncoated stock shifts the ramp cooler and flattens the violet end. Proof on the stock, not on a house sheet.
  • Flat bands are the failure mode of a long gradient on paper. Keep any one flat under an inch at the size it is printed.
  • No placed image has an upper quartile above gold, L 0.781. Checked on the file, not on the proof.
  • No varnish or foil on the fall. A specular finish reverses the one rule wherever the light catches it.

Voice

Unhurried and physical. It names heat, light, breath and skin.

It describes a sequence, because the product is a sequence. Certain without pushing: the brand does not argue for itself, and assumes you will understand it if you are shown it in the right order.

Where the rules stop

Cart, checkout, shipping notices, legal and safety copy are plain and fast. The atmosphere stops there on purpose, exactly as the voice does. Applied to a payment form or a warning label the discipline makes it worse.

Elsewhere

The full voice, the word lists and the tone by context live in voice-tone.md. Event art direction for the launch is in the brief and governs that night only; nothing in it binds the brand.
